scope: Primary-source context for candidate mechanisms; none of these papers validates the selected 2024 emission residual as atmospheric variability.

sources.title: KELT-9 b's Asymmetric TESS Transit Caused by Rapid Stellar Rotation and Spin-Orbit Misalignment
sources.finding: The inferred oblate, gravity-darkened star gives wavelength-dependent irradiation that varies twice per orbit; the reported orbital modulation is about 10 percent in the UV and 1 to 2 percent in the optical.
sources.application: Motivates a directional and phase-dependent stellar boundary absent from the fixed uniform PHOENIX input. The separate 1.07-percent endpoint-change estimate assumes a sinusoid with 10-percent peak-to-peak modulation; it is not this paper's reconstructed curve or a bound on atmospheric nonlinear response.

sources.title: The stable climate of KELT-9b
sources.finding: The phase-curve analysis accounts for roughly 7.5-hour stellar pulsations. Repeated broad-band occultations show no detected brightness-temperature variability above their approximately one-percent sensitivity.
sources.application: Motivates stellar time-dependent controls. Broad-band stability does not constrain a narrow H-alpha residual to one percent, and photometric pulsation amplitude is not a line-depth or line-width amplitude.

sources.title: Rapid escape of ultra-hot exoplanet atmospheres driven by Hydrogen Balmer absorption
sources.finding: Excited hydrogen absorbs the strong near-UV irradiation of hot stars and can drive escape through Balmer-continuum heating.
sources.application: Excited-state photoionization, recombination and thermal feedback already exist in this repository. Changing their spatial irradiation or coupled populations is a new hypothesis; adding the same channel again would double count it.

sources.title: Aeronomy of the upper atmosphere of KELT-9 b
sources.section: Abstract and discussion of optically thick recombination
sources.finding: A three-dimensional model combines Roche geometry, excited-state kinetics and irradiation to compare H-alpha, H-beta, Paschen-beta and oxygen transit absorption. Reionization and trapped resonance photons can reduce the effective rate of final recombination.
sources.application: Supports examining multidimensional density/velocity/excitation together and warns against equating a gross recombination time with population relaxation. A transit absorption fit does not establish an emission-phase solution here.

sources.title: The formation of the H-alpha line in the solar chromosphere
sources.finding: Three-dimensional solar calculations find that H-alpha can be synthesized in statistical equilibrium and complete redistribution when the underlying atmosphere includes non-equilibrium hydrogen ionization and the Lyman lines use an appropriate profile treatment.
sources.application: Frequency redistribution and ionization history merit a qualified audit, especially through Lyman-line control of n=2. This solar result neither validates the planetary approximation nor supports claiming that direct H-alpha partial redistribution must fix the observed trough.

sources.title: Multi-epoch detections of the extended atmosphere and transmission spectra of KELT-9b with a 1.5 m telescope
sources.finding: Multi-epoch H-alpha transit observations were examined with asymmetric extended-gas geometries; a tail interpretation requires substantial excited hydrogen at large distances.
sources.application: Motivates spatially selective absorption as a hypothesis with a population-maintenance requirement. A screen in the pure-absorption limit can lower an intrinsic core but cannot create blue emission. The geometry is not established for these emission exposures.

implementation_distinction: Current observer rays resolve projected radial, rotation and prescribed zonal velocities; a spatially varying atmospheric equilibrium is not thereby solved.
The atmosphere has eight physical radial cells. Observer quadrature refinement does not qualify convergence of the physical stratification or finite atom.
The tested full spherical H-alpha coupling already increased upper emission and worsened the earlier native comparison; it is not a newly promising extra loss channel.
A cool or partially covering layer requires an excitation and energy budget; source suppression is a diagnostic condition, not an independently tunable physical state.
